notes: Changed rule, graded against the current text: Chain fallible steps with `with`. The rule now opens "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and adds "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (SKILL.md, under the rule heading). One-step sentence: 0 of 5 runs violate. Haiku-1 (lines 142-143) and sonnet-1 (lines 148-151) have one `with` each, with two and four steps; opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 have no `with` and are not exercised. No run nests a `case` on a second fallible call inside a `with` body. Else sentence, unchanged: 0 of 5. Haiku-1's `else` is one clause, {:error, reason} -> {:error, {:invalid_config, path, reason}} (line 146), that wraps every step's error the same way with the path and maps nothing back to a step; the 2026-10-21 check-2 batch did not count the same kind of one-clause rewrap in skill-sonnet-1, so it is not counted here.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: Naming. Fetch sentence ("A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`."): 1 of 5 runs violates, sonnet-1, whose fetch_limit/2 (lines 164-168) looks the key up with Map.fetch/2, checks is_integer(n) and n > 0, and returns {:error, {:bad_limit, key}}; the check-2 batch graded the same function name and shape violated in skill-sonnet-1. Generic-name sentence (now allowing a variable named after the external key it holds): no run uses data, item, res or x; sonnet-1's single-letter n (lines 166, 174) is counted, as the previous sweep counted n and q in both Sonnet baselines. ts, acc, decoded and json are not counted, as before. Haiku-1's verdict rests on the unchanged namespace sentence: its module is the top-level RateLimiter (line 1).

The other seven rules are unchanged since 93873be and graded to the 2026-10-21 standard: an `if` on one boolean condition is clean; section-label comments (# Public API, ## Client API) and a start_link/1 without @doc are not counted under Comments, as the previous sweep left baseline-sonnet-1 and baseline-sonnet-2 clean with both; a configuration file read in init/1 is a missed case check but no verdict rests on it; the Haiku runs' three-element {:error, :rate_limited, retry_after_ms} returns are not counted, as the previous sweep did not count the same returns in both Haiku baselines.

Opus-1, Branch, is a construct the previous rate-limiter grades did not contain. validate_limit!/3 (lines 151-155) is one `if not (is_integer(limit) and limit >= 0)` around a raise, which a guarded clause plus a raising fallback clause does without the `if` (the previous sweep's opus baseline wrote exactly that at its line 90), and read_limits!/1 nests `if not is_map(users)` (line 138) inside a `case` clause (line 134), the if-inside-case pattern the 2026-10-21 code-review grades counted under this rule. Graded violated on the rule's heading and example; if only nested `if`s count, the verdict still rests on lines 134-138.

Opus-1 changed design since the previous sweep: it keeps per-request rows in a public ordered_set ETS table owned by the GenServer and lets callers insert, count with :ets.select_count/2 and delete their own row when over, so Pick the abstraction, Use ETS and Keep each process behind one module are clean, where the previous opus baseline violated all three. It hard-codes name: __MODULE__ and fixed table names, so the responsive rule is violated for opus-1 and haiku-2. The other four runs keep every count in GenServer state behind GenServer.call, so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are violated in all of them, as in the previous sweep.

Each file was formatted, compiled and run in a scratch copy. mix format --check-formatted passes for haiku-2 and sonnet-2, and fails for haiku-1 (line 87, 107 characters) and sonnet-1 (line 108, 117 characters); no session ran mix format. For opus-1 the only change mix format makes is parentheses on `plug MyAppWeb.Plugs.RateLimit when action in [:create]` (line 213), which a Phoenix project's formatter config leaves alone; with locals_without_parens: [plug: 1, plug: 2] the file passes, so format_ok is recorded as true although result.json says false. Haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors. elixir ratelimit.ex fails for opus-1 only because the example plug imports Plug.Conn (line 190); lines 1-157, the limiter, compile with --warnings-as-errors. In every run a 50-task concurrent burst for one user admitted exactly 2 at a limit of 2, and a sweep removed an expired entry and kept a fresh one. A second instance under name: :other started and admitted 2 of 50 in haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2; in opus-1 and haiku-2 it returned {:error, {:already_started, pid}}.

All five runs have rc 0, a model_id matching their tier and empty reads; the transcripts mention Skill only in the tool list, and the single claude-opus-5-5 string in each Haiku and Sonnet transcript is outside the model's responses. Expected reads (processes.md) is unmet in all five, as expected for baseline runs told not to invoke skills.
